description: The WRITE half of the S395 §17.6.2 arm-body ruling at the two positions that remain POSITIVELY assertable after S397. `#out-recovery` asserts that a bindless `!{}` recovery in a then-arm is a SIDE EFFECT — it does not designate the arm's result, so the arm still evaluates to its `lift` (the sixth repoint site of the class). `#out-lift-literal` is the value-form CONTROL: the identical arm shape with a literal renders `41`, which is what keeps a companion empty/absent render discriminating rather than vacuous. ⛑ THE THREE `~`-READING FUNCTIONS THAT USED TO LIVE HERE HAVE MOVED, NOT BEEN DELETED — see `ctrl-028-arm-body-tilde-read-orphan-neg`, which carries them VERBATIM.
rationale: Companion to ctrl-025 / ctrl-026, which pin the same WRITE half at the bare-statement and nested-value-form-declaration positions. ⛑ S397 RE-SCOPE, AND THE REASON IS A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, NOT A GREEN-SUITE CONVENIENCE. This case previously carried three functions whose arm body read a bare `~` (`record(~)` in a then-arm, the same in an else-arm, and `lift ~`), and it PINNED THE ORPHAN SIDE of that read: `#out-lift-tilde` asserted `text: ""`, because codegen's `~` pre-scan allocates no slot for an enclosing sequence that mentions `~` nowhere outside the arm, and `emitIdent` then returned `null /* ~ orphaned — codegen-fallback */`. S397 replaced that fallback with `E-CG-TILDE-UNRESOLVED` (Error). All three shapes are therefore now REJECTED, and a rejected program has no DOM to anchor — so the pin cannot survive on the positive side in any form. ⚑ Per §62.2 the corpus IS the versioned language contract, so the three functions were MOVED VERBATIM into a new `-neg` case rather than edited or dropped: every source shape this case ever carried is still in the corpus, each now pinned to the contract that actually governs it. The information content is preserved and sharpened — `text: ""` said only "something rendered nothing", while the neg case names the code, its severity, and its exact cardinality. What is NOT claimed here: that the arm-body `~` READ question is settled. It is not; it is dpa-040, and S397 landed only its floor. The two functions that remain contain no `~` at all and are unaffected by that fork in either direction, which is precisely why they stayed. `notCodePrefixes` keeps `E-TILDE-` and `E-CG-` because neither shape below reads `~`; if either ever draws a tilde-family or codegen-family diagnostic, that is a regression in the recovery or value-form lowering, not a `~` question.
